title: Pick a start
goal: I can choose a way to start a puzzle, and check my answer against every clue.

learn.intro: Choose a start: draw a model, make a list or a table, work backwards, guess and check, or use a logic grid. Then check your answer against every clue.

example.problem: Ali, Mei and Siti each have a different pet: a dog, a cat or a fish. Ali does not have a fish. Mei does not have a cat or a fish. Who has the cat?
steps: Mei does not have a cat or a fish, so Mei has the dog. Write Yes for Mei and dog.
The dog is taken. Write No in the dog column for Ali and Siti, and No in the other columns for Mei.
Ali has no fish and no dog, so Ali has the cat.
Check: Siti has the fish. Every clue is true.

howto.title: How to
steps: Use a clue that tells you something for sure.
A Yes means No in the rest of its row and column.
Check every clue at the end.

facts.title: Ways to start
lines: List in order or make a table.

try.text: Ben, Kumar and Aisha each choose a different drink: tea, juice or milk. Ben does not choose juice or milk. Aisha does not choose tea. Kumar does not choose milk. Who chooses juice? {b}
try.explanation: Ben cannot have juice or milk, so Ben has tea. Kumar does not choose milk and tea is taken, so Kumar has juice. Aisha has the milk. All clues are true.

items.text: Mei picks a number. She multiplies it by 3, adds 8 and then halves the result. She gets 19. What number did Mei pick? {b}
items.explanation: Work backwards, undoing the last step first. Undo halve: 19 × 2 = 38. Undo add 8: 38 - 8 = 30. Undo multiply by 3: 30 ÷ 3 = 10.

items.text: Kumar spends 1/4 of his money. Then he spends $6. He has $15 left. How much money did Kumar have at first? $ {b}
items.explanation: Before the $6: $21 = 3/4 of the money. 1/4 = $7, so $28.

items.text: Aisha, Wei and Ravi own a turtle, a parrot and a goldfish, one each. Ravi owns neither the parrot nor the goldfish. Aisha does not own the goldfish. Who owns the parrot? {b}
items.explanation: Ravi has the turtle. Aisha does not have the goldfish, so she has the parrot.

items.text: Two numbers add up to 52. The larger number is 14 more than the smaller number.
items.explanation: Take away the 14: 52 - 14 = 38. Share equally: 19 and 19. Add the 14 back to one of them: 33 and 19.

items.text: Count the squares of every size in a 3 by 3 grid.

Exactly one of 3 children broke a vase. Exactly one of the 3 children is telling the truth.
Ali says, "I did not break the vase."
Ben says, "Ali broke the vase."
Siti says, "Ben is lying." Who broke the vase? {b}
items.explanation: If Ali broke it: 1 truth (Ben). If Ben broke it: 2 truths. If Siti broke it: 2 truths. Only Ali fits.

items.text: Dad is 40 years old. Ali is 8 years old. In how many years will Dad be 3 times as old as Ali? {b} years
items.explanation: The age difference stays 32. When Dad is 3 times as old, Ali is 16: 8 years from now.

items.text: Ben gives 1/3 of his stickers to Ali. He gives 1/2 of the rest to Mei. 12 stickers are left. Find the number of stickers Ben began with. {b}
items.explanation: Work backwards. The 12 left are half of the rest, so the rest was 24. The 24 is 2/3 of his stickers, so 1/3 is 12 and he had 36.

items.text: A farm has hens and cows, 20 animals in all. They have 56 legs altogether. Hens have 2 legs each and cows have 4 legs each.
items.explanation: All hens: 40 legs, 16 short. Each cow adds 2: 8 cows, 12 hens.

items.text: The product of 2 whole numbers is 72. Their sum is 17. List the pairs with product 72 to find them.
items.explanation: Pairs with product 72 have sums 73, 38, 27, 22, 18, 17. Only 8 and 9 give 17.

items.text: Use the digit cards 1, 2 and 3 once each to make 3-digit numbers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of different numbers is {b}.

items.text: Ali writes the whole numbers from 1 to 60. How many times does he write the digit 5? {b}
items.explanation: Ones place: 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55 is 6. Tens place: 50 to 59 is 10. Total 16.

items.text:
Ben, Kumar, Aisha and Wei each play a different sport: swimming, tennis, football or badminton. Write Yes or No in the grid. Then write the sport for each child.
Clue 1: Ben does not play tennis or badminton.
Clue 2: Kumar does not play swimming or tennis.
Clue 3: Wei does not play swimming, badminton or tennis.
items.hint: Which child has the most clues? Start with Wei.
items.explanation: Wei: football. Ben: swimming. Kumar: badminton. Aisha: tennis.

items.text: Count the squares and the rectangles in a 2 by 4 grid. A square also counts as a rectangle.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of squares (all sizes) is {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The number of rectangles (all sizes) is {b}.

items.hint: Count by size: 1 by 1, 2 by 1, 3 by 1, 4 by 1 ... and then 2 high.

items.text: In a cafe, 1/4 of the customers leave. Then 3 more customers arrive. Then 1/3 of the customers in the cafe leave. 14 customers are left. How many customers were in the cafe at first? {b}
items.hint: Undo the last step first. 14 is what part of the number before?

items.text: For how many 3-digit numbers do the digits sum to 7? Make an ordered list to be sure. {b}
items.hint: Sort by the first digit: 1__, 2__, ... How many for each?
items.explanation: By hundreds digit 1 to 7: 7 + 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 28.

items.text: Ali has 24 coins. They are 10¢, 20¢ and 50¢ coins. The number of 10¢ coins equals the number of 50¢ coins. The coins are worth $7.00 in all.
items.hint: Join a 10¢ coin and a 50¢ coin as a pair. How much is a pair?
items.explanation: A 10¢ and 50¢ pair is 60¢. All 20¢ is $4.80, $2.20 short. A pair in place of two 20¢ coins adds 20¢: 11 pairs. 24 - 22 = 2 coins of 20¢.

items.text: A drawer has 10 red socks, 10 blue socks and 10 black socks. You take socks out in the dark. How many socks must you take to be sure of 2 socks of the same colour? {b}
items.hint: Think of the worst luck. How many socks can you take with no pair?
items.explanation: Worst case: 1 red, 1 blue, 1 black, no pair. The 4th sock matches one.

items.text: Siti picks a number. She adds 7 and then multiplies by 4. She gets 60. What number did Siti pick? {b}
items.explanation: Work backwards. Undo multiply by 4: 60 ÷ 4 = 15. Undo add 7: 15 - 7 = 8.

items.text: Mei spends 2/5 of her money. Then she spends $9. She has $12 left. How much money did Mei have at first? $ {b}
items.explanation: Before the $9 she had $12 + $9 = $21. The $21 is 3/5 of her money, so 1/5 is $7 and the whole is 5 × $7 = $35.

items.text: A box holds 9 hens and goats. They have 26 legs altogether. A hen has 2 legs and a goat has 4 legs. How many goats are there? {b}
items.explanation: Suppose all 9 are hens: 18 legs. That is 26 - 18 = 8 legs short. Each goat adds 2 legs, so 8 ÷ 2 = 4 goats.

items.text: Count the squares of every size in a 2 by 3 grid. {b}
items.explanation: There are 6 small squares. A 2 by 2 square can go in 2 places. 6 + 2 = 8.
